method: Opened official agency/legal pages and inspected relevant passages with web tool; no third-party teaching source used
changes_to_manuscript: G1 Chapter 1 additions; previous source checks remain dated 4 October 2026

sources.finding: Category B mass/age/residence/permit/test requirements; practice ages, approved supervisor, proof and visible learner sign. Exceptions retained.
Course requirement ended 1 August 2026; individual supervisor approval still required.
Two mandatory parts before tests, valid until licence obtained or at most five years; motorcycle training does not substitute.
TSFS 2026:47 sets one-year validity from 19 August 2026; earlier tests retain earlier provisions.
Trafikverket confirms four months before 19 August and one year from that date; automated-transmission restriction also supported.
Traffic Regulation chapter 2 section 1, chapter 3 sections 1 and 14: care, fitness and adapting speed.
0.2 per mille alcohol threshold; aggravated factors include 1.0, substantial impairment or clear danger; non-prescribed narcotics zero tolerance.
Attention/vision/reaction/coordination effects, next-day impairment and prescribed-drug impairment responsibility.
Medical eligibility assessment for permit; distinct from daily fitness to drive.
TSFS 2011:20 chapters 4–5 support journey choices, personal/social pressures and reflection. No exam guarantees added.
Trafikverket supports allowing time, rest breaks, traffic/road-condition checks and seasonal preparation.

G1_sources.title: Nollvisionen – tillsammans räddar vi liv
G1_sources.excerpt: På sikt ska ingen dödas eller allvarligt skadas inom vägtransportsystemet
G1_sources.supports: No deaths or serious injuries in the road transport system; shared responsibility of road users and system designers

G1_sources.title: Drowsy Driving
G1_sources.version: Live page; publication date not displayed in retrieved passage
G1_sources.locator: Tips to Drive Alert: How To Avoid Driving Drowsy item 1; Short-Term Interventions item 1
G1_sources.excerpt: Getting adequate sleep on a daily basis is the only true way
G1_sources.supports: Adequate sleep is fundamental; coffee/energy drinks can give temporary perceived alertness without preventing microsleep in serious sleep deprivation
G1_sources.fallback_reason: Exact sleep-remedy and temporary-alertness distinction not located in inspected TS/TRV pages; general physiological advice applies in Sweden; US speeds and recommendations not imported.

G1_sources.title: Microsleeps — Module 3, Negative Impacts on Sleep
G1_sources.version: Last reviewed 31 March 2020; Module 3, page 3 of 28
G1_sources.excerpt: involuntary episodes of sleep lasting a few seconds
G1_sources.supports: Brief unintended sleep; general physiological definition, not an occupational driving rule
G1_sources.fallback_reason: Exact definition not located in inspected TS/TRV material; proposed VTI lead did not yield a retrievable exact definition.

G1_sources.publisher: Swedish Government; published by Sveriges riksdag
G1_sources.title: Drograttfylleri och sjöfylleri — proposition 1998/99:43
G1_sources.locator: Printed page 24, paragraph beginning De centralstimulerande medlen
G1_sources.excerpt: kan framkalla påtagligt höjt självförtroende i förening med hyperaktivitet
G1_sources.supports: Amphetamine/cocaine can increase confidence while concentration and clear thinking are impaired
G1_sources.fallback_reason: TRV alcohol/drug overview and TS substance reports give general impairment background but not this exact confidence claim. Historical passage used only for physiological effects, never current legal rules or obsolete warning-label advice.

G1_sources.title: Drugs and Human Performance Fact Sheets
G1_sources.locator: Printed pages 62–64 (PDF pages 63–65), Methamphetamine, Effects / Performance Effects / Effects on Driving
G1_sources.excerpt: reduced fatigue or drowsiness, increased alertness
G1_sources.supports: Perceived fatigue can diminish while risk-taking and driving impairment remain; fatigue and sleepiness may follow as drug effects change
G1_sources.fallback_reason: Exact masking claim not located in inspected TS/TRV sources. Historical pharmacology summary supports a qualified can statement about stimulant misuse, not every prescribed dose or every stimulant.
